summary.intent: Execute all 9 plans of phase 71 (Share-Invite Security & IPNS Data-Integrity API) in dependency-ordered waves using parallel subagent executors, per the execute-phase orchestrator workflow, with no CLI flags active.
summary.outcome: Waves 1, 2, and 3a (7 of 9 plans: 71-01, 71-02, 71-03, 71-04, 71-06, 71-07, 71-08) executed, merged, and post-merge gates passed green (typecheck, cargo check --all-targets, 889/889 api tests); the checkpoint plan 71-05 (live-stack race test) and Wave 4 (71-09) remained pending when the transcript ends, with the Wave 3a tracking commit failing to land and being retried.

repo: Phase 71 worktrees fork from live HEAD (baseRef reason `baseref-head`), so all 4 waves retain parallel worktree isolation with no inter-wave degrade

Root `pnpm typecheck` is the real cross-plan integration check for this monorepo, but it intentionally fails mid-phase (Wave 1 renames the API while sdk/web consumers are only fixed in Wave 2) — post-merge gates must be scoped per-wave to what actually reached a consistent state rather than always running the full command

`apps/api tsc --noEmit` is NOT covered by the root `pnpm typecheck` CI script and is not CI-gated — pre-existing errors there (crypto/dist staleness cascade, ipns-verify-cache.spec.ts TS2352, http-metrics.interceptor.spec.ts TS2724 HttpArgumentsHost) are non-blocking noise, not regressions
`packages/crypto` dist can be stale in fresh worktrees, causing spurious null-narrowing/type errors downstream (apps/api) until `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/crypto build` is run
This phase's requirement IDs use CONTEXT.md decision-ID naming (e.g. D-10, D-04), not the global REQUIREMENTS.md REQ-ID scheme, so `requirements.mark-complete` is a no-op for phase-71 plans
`npx jest --testPathPattern=...` should be used directly instead of `pnpm --filter test --`, which silently drops the pattern arg due to double `--` wrapping

codebase-drift gate flags ~143 pre-existing structural elements as advisory noise whenever `last_mapped_commit` is null (repo never `/gsd-map-codebase`'d) — not a real regression signal until the repo is mapped once

code.finding: Agent-reported E0560 diagnostic referencing old descriptor field names was stale LSP/intermediate-worktree noise, not a real error — cargo check --all-targets on the merged tree compiled cleanly
Same stale-diagnostic pattern as delete.rs:543-546; resolved as non-issue after merge

Modified by 71-04 (D-05 same-seq CID equivocation guard, D-06 23505→409 ConflictException translation); null-narrowing errors initially attributed here by 71-08 were actually a crypto/dist staleness cascade, not a real regression from this file

71-07 replaced claimInvite's existing-share log-and-return with a widen-only merge (isWriteUpgrade/isGenerationBump gates) inside the existing claim transaction, preserving never-downgrade write→read invariant (T-66-E1)

71-08 replaced revokeForItems's manager.find(Share)+manager.remove(shares) with a single createQueryBuilder().delete().from(Share) scoped to sharer_id + share_root_ipns_name, mirroring the sibling invite-revoke .update() block

workflow: Orchestrator dispatches wave agents one at a time (not all at once) and verifies each new agent's worktree was created before dispatching the next, to avoid a config.lock race on worktree creation

Post-merge gates should re-verify diagnostics an executor subagent flags rather than trusting them at face value — run the authoritative check (e.g. cargo check --all-targets) against the actually-merged tree before deciding a fix is needed
Known false-negative: the tracking-commit helper can report `commit_failed` even when the commit actually lands — verify via `git log`/git state before trusting the reported status
STATE.md/ROADMAP.md writes are intentionally reserved for the orchestrator; executor subagents must not modify them, only leave SUMMARY.md files

friction: 71-03's task-notification result included a misleading E0560 Rust compile diagnostic that turned out to be stale/inaccurate, requiring an extra verification pass at the Wave 2 post-merge gate
71-08 surfaced pre-existing tsc --noEmit errors that needed manual classification (pre-existing vs. phase-introduced) via git diff against origin/main and CI config inspection
Wave 3a's tracking commit did not land on the first attempt (ROADMAP.md remained staged, HEAD unchanged), requiring a retry with more visible output

71-02 (TS consumers rename) took ~95 minutes and could not run sdk-e2e suites end-to-end against a live API stack in its worktree (no docker stack available), leaving that verification deferred to before merge

Wave 4 (71-09: restore invite-service unit coverage) not yet started, depends on 71-06 and 71-07 which are now merged
